_comment: SHARED dual-transport fixture for the eBird checklist-id shape guard
(backend-guard-anchor-parity). Loaded by BOTH
frontend/src/lib/checklistId.parity.test.ts and
backend/tests/test_checklist_id_parity.py, so if either twin drifts its own
test fails.
Python  services/ebird.py              CHECKLIST_ID_RE = ^S[0-9]+$
JS      lib/checklistId.ts             isValidChecklistId (gates the
REQUEST: App.tsx checks it before
fetching /weather/{id}, /tide/{id})
JS      components/speciesDetail/ui.tsx SUBMISSION_ID_RE (gates the LINK)
Before this change the Python half was two byte-identical copies inside
routers/weather.py and routers/tide.py; it is now one constant. The JS side
is NOT single-sourced and this change does not make it so: the two guards
above, plus four more copies of the same literal in lib/mediaStats.ts,
lib/speciesStats.ts, map/TargetMarkers.tsx and map/NearbyLiferMarkers.tsx,
are all byte-identical today. Consolidating them is separate work. The
vitest half therefore drives BOTH of the guards above and asserts they agree
with each other, so neither can drift away from the backend unnoticed.
CHARACTER CLASSES are the half this pair shipped divergent on. Python's `\d`
matches every Unicode decimal digit (category Nd) while JavaScript's `\d` is
ASCII-only, so an id of S followed by U+0660 U+0661 U+0662 (Arabic-Indic 012)
passed the backend guard and failed the frontend one.
The Python side therefore writes an EXPLICIT ASCII CLASS ([0-9]), and the
rows below carry three separate Nd blocks (Arabic-Indic, fullwidth,
Devanagari) plus a mixed ASCII/non-ASCII id, because any of them alone would
leave a `\d` regression passing on two thirds of the probe set.
ANCHORS are the other half, and on THIS pair they already agreed: both sides
use whole-string matching (`re.fullmatch` / `^...$` with `.test()`), so every
newline row below is expected to fail on both transports BEFORE and AFTER the
class fix. They are here because the house rule says every twinned pattern
gets trailing-, leading- and embedded-newline rows, and because they are the
evidence that the character-class bug and the anchor bug fixed in the same
change are genuinely two defects and not one: swapping the anchor here
changes nothing, exactly as swapping the class in settingskv.py changes
nothing.
Exotic characters are written as \uXXXX ESCAPES, never literals: this repo
has had literal exotic whitespace and digits silently flattened into ordinary
ASCII four times across two builds, leaving a probe set weaker with every
test still green. Both non-vacuity tests pin the code points directly, so a
flattened escape fails rather than quietly narrowing the fixture.

cases.why: the ordinary case: a real eBird submission id
minimal valid id, one digit
leading zeros are digits like any other; nothing normalizes them away
a long but well-formed id stays valid (the guard bounds shape, not length)
ARABIC-INDIC DIGITS: the v0.5.54 trap and the discriminating row of this change. Python's `\d` admits U+0660..U+0662, JavaScript's does not
FULLWIDTH DIGITS (U+FF10..U+FF12): a second Nd block, so a `\d` regression cannot pass by handling only Arabic-Indic
DEVANAGARI DIGITS (U+0966..U+0968): a third Nd block
MIXED ASCII and Arabic-Indic: the nastiest shape, since the id looks well-formed up to its last character
CYRILLIC CAPITAL DZE (U+0405) renders like an S but is not one; the literal `S` is ASCII on both sides
ANCHOR row: a trailing newline. Expected false on BOTH transports before and after this change, because both already match the whole string
ANCHOR row: a leading newline
ANCHOR row: an embedded newline cannot smuggle a valid id past either engine
a trailing carriage return is the other line terminator and is rejected the same way
no digits at all
no leading S
lowercase s is not the shape eBird emits
a doubled prefix
punctuation inside the digits
an interior space
trailing whitespace is not trimmed into a valid id
a trailing tab (U+0009), written as an escape so it cannot be flattened
the empty string
the location-id prefix must not be accepted by the checklist guard
a path separator can never become part of an id
